section_1.title: The Ternary Bridge (Prerequisite Concept)
section_1.content: Introduce the base-3 (ternary) numbering system as the foundation. Contrast it with binary to explain how ternary 'digits' (0, 1, 2) naturally represent three-way branching paths or three-peg systems.
section_1.example: A smart lock that requires a 3-digit ternary code to open, visualizing the sequence 0-1-2 as transitions between states.

section_2.title: The Constrained Towers of Hanoi
section_2.content: Introduce the 'Adjacent-Only' constraint: disks can only move to an adjacent peg. Explain how this restriction forces a sequence of moves that mimics a recursive pattern, mapping directly to ternary counting.
section_2.example: A robot arm restricted to moving a disk only to the immediate left or right peg; show that moving a 3-disk tower requires exactly 3^n - 1 steps.

section_3.title: Mapping Moves to the Sierpinski Triangle
section_3.content: Visually map the sequence of legal moves in the constrained Hanoi puzzle onto the edges of a Sierpinski triangle. Each level of the triangle represents the state space of the disks.
section_3.example: An animation of a disk-moving path that traces the perimeter of a growing Sierpinski fractal as the number of disks increases.

section_4.title: Unified Synthesis & Conclusion
section_4.content: Summarize how the ternary representation, the movement constraints, and the fractal geometry are isomorphic. The 'state' of the tower is simply a coordinate in a 2D fractal space.
section_4.example: A final visual showing the 'Hanoi path' drawing the Sierpinski triangle in real-time, demonstrating that mathematics is just the discovery of these hidden structural symmetries.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 1.5 + j * 0.8
                y = 2.2 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Ternary Bridge", [
            "Ternary systems use three digits: zero, one, two.", 
            "Each digit represents a unique branching path state.", 
            "These represent transitions between three logical pegs."
        ])
        
        c0 = Circle(radius=0.4, color="#FF5733", fill_opacity=0.6)
        c1 = Circle(radius=0.4, color="#33FF57", fill_opacity=0.6)
        c2 = Circle(radius=0.4, color="#3357FF", fill_opacity=0.6)
        
        l0 = Text("0", font_size=24).move_to(c0.get_center())
        l1 = Text("1", font_size=24).move_to(c1.get_center())
        l2 = Text("2", font_size=24).move_to(c2.get_center())
        
        node0 = VGroup(c0, l0)
        node1 = VGroup(c1, l1)
        node2 = VGroup(c2, l2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF5733"), run_time=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(node0, "B2")
        self.place_at_grid(node1, "B4")
        self.place_at_grid(node2, "B6")
        self.play(FadeIn(node0), FadeIn(node1), FadeIn(node2))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#33FF57"), run_time=0.5)
        path = CurvedArrow(node0.get_center(), node1.get_center(), angle=-TAU/6)
        self.play(Create(path))
        self.play(FadeOut(path))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#3357FF"), run_time=0.5)
        # Visualizing transitions
        self.play(node0.animate.move_to(self.grid["D2"]), run_time=0.5)
